articles.title: Women Focus: BJP Plans ₹20,000 Direct Transfer for Women Voters Ahead of UP Elections
articles.description: The BJP is reportedly preparing a major financial assistance initiative targeting women voters ahead of the upcoming Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections. According to sources cited in the report, the proposed plan involves transferring ₹20,000 directly into the bank accounts of eligible women. The target is reportedly around 3.6 crore women across the state. Sources suggest that the Uttar Pradesh BJP organisation and the state government have made preparations for the proposed scheme, but its implementation is still awaiting approval from the party's central leadership. If the proposal receives the green signal, a budget provision could be introduced during the upcoming winter session of the Uttar Pradesh Assembly. The funds would reportedly be transferred directly to women's bank accounts once the necessary budgetary approval is secured. However, the announcement and implementation of the scheme are not yet confirmed. The proposal is being viewed as a significant part of the BJP's preparations to strengthen its support among women voters before the state elections. The next major development will depend on the central leadership's approval and the government's decision on the budget allocation.

articles.title: Punjab Politics: BJP-Akali Dal Alliance May Reshape the State's Political Equations
articles.description: The proposed BJP-Shiromani Akali Dal alliance could reshape Punjab's political equations after six years apart. According to the discussion, the two parties governed Punjab together from 2007 to 2017 and reportedly secured a combined vote share of around 41–45% in the 2017 Assembly election. However, after contesting separately in 2022, both parties suffered a major decline in their electoral performance. The alliance is being seen as important for rebuilding the Akali Dal's traditional rural and Panthic support base, while the BJP hopes to expand its influence in Punjab. The discussion also highlights the emergence of groups such as Waris Punjab De and the reorganisation of Panthic voters who have moved away from the Akali Dal. Questions remain over whether these groups will consolidate their political influence or whether traditional parties will regain that support. The BJP is reportedly seeking a larger share of Assembly seats this time, citing its performance in the 2024 Lok Sabha election. It secured around 18.65% of the vote in Punjab, compared with approximately 13.5% for the Akali Dal. The BJP may focus on urban constituencies, while the Akali Dal seeks to rebuild its rural base. The alliance could pose a challenge to both the Aam Aadmi Party and Congress, although AAP's welfare schemes, including free electricity and financial assistance for women, remain important factors in rural Punjab.

articles.title: Japan's Missiles On Indian Soil? Why New Defence Pact Threatens China's Indo-Pacific Dominance
articles.description: China has spent years expanding its naval presence across the Indo-Pacific. Now India and Japan are strengthening a defence partnership that could change regional military calculations. A new understanding would allow Japanese forces to conduct missile training at Indian firing ranges, while India could gain access to advanced Japanese stealth-warship technology. The two countries are also exploring stronger naval logistics and ship-repair cooperation. For New Delhi, the arrangement could expand operational options beyond the Indian Ocean. For Tokyo, it offers access to valuable military training infrastructure and a major strategic partner. Beijing faces border tensions with India and maritime disputes with Japan, making their growing cooperation strategically significant. But this is not a formal military alliance. It is a bilateral effort to improve military readiness, industrial cooperation and regional security. This report explains the agreements, the China factor and the changing Indo-Pacific power equation.
